string-array.name: descriptionNeckWeightedLateralNeckFlexion
string-array.item: Weighted Lateral Neck Flexion
A strengthening exercise targeting the lateral neck muscles, ideal for improving neck stability and mobility.
To perform the exercise:
1. Secure a neck harness with a weight attached to the side of your head.
2. Sit or stand upright, keeping your back straight and shoulders relaxed.
3. Slowly tilt your head towards the side with the weight, stretching the opposite side of your neck.
4. Return your head to the starting position and repeat for the desired repetitions before switching sides.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Perform the movement in a controlled manner to avoid straining the neck muscles.
2. Keep your movements slow and focused to maintain tension on the target muscles.

string-array.name: descriptionNeckWeightedLyingNeckExtension
string-array.item: Weighted Lying Neck Extension
A neck-strengthening exercise that targets the posterior neck muscles to improve neck stability and posture.
To perform the exercise:
1. Lie face down on a flat bench with your head hanging off the edge.
2. Place a lightweight plate on the back of your head, holding it in place with your hands.
3. Slowly lift your head upwards by extending your neck, keeping the motion controlled.
4. Lower your head back to the starting position and repeat for the desired repetitions.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Start with a light weight to avoid straining your neck.
2. Keep your movements controlled to maintain tension on the posterior neck muscles.

string-array.name: descriptionNeckWeightedLyingNeckFlexion
string-array.item: Weighted Lying Neck Flexion
This exercise targets the anterior neck muscles, improving neck strength and reducing injury risk.
To perform the exercise:
1. Lie on your back on a flat bench with your head hanging off the edge.
2. Place a lightweight plate on your forehead, holding it securely with your hands.
3. Slowly lower your head backwards, stretching the neck muscles.
4. Flex your neck to lift your head back to the starting position and repeat for the desired repetitions.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Use a light weight and progress gradually as your neck strength improves.
2. Avoid jerky movements to reduce strain on the neck.

string-array.name: descriptionNeckGittlesonShrug
string-array.item: Gittleson Shrug
A unique exercise targeting the trapezius and upper shoulder muscles for improved strength and posture.
To perform the exercise:
1. Stand upright with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing your body.
2. Shrug your shoulders upwards as high as possible, focusing on engaging the trapezius.
3. Hold the top position briefly, then lower your shoulders back down and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Perform slow and controlled movements to maximize engagement of the trapezius muscles.
2. Avoid rotating your shoulders during the exercise to maintain proper form.

string-array.name: descriptionNeckDiagonalNeckStretch
string-array.item: Diagonal Neck Stretch
A stretching exercise to target the neck and upper shoulder muscles, relieving tension and improving flexibility.
To perform the exercise:
1. Sit or stand upright with your shoulders relaxed.
2. Tilt your head diagonally forward, bringing your ear toward the opposite shoulder.
3. Gently place your hand on the side of your head to enhance the stretch.
4. Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds, then switch sides and repeat.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Avoid using excessive force to pull your head to prevent strain.
2. Keep your shoulders relaxed throughout the stretch.

string-array.name: descriptionNeckNeckRotationStretch
string-array.item: Neck Rotation Stretch
A simple and effective stretch to improve neck mobility and alleviate tension in the cervical spine.
To perform the exercise:
1. Sit or stand upright with your shoulders relaxed and back straight.
2. Slowly turn your head to one side, looking over your shoulder.
3. Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds, then return to the center and switch sides.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Move your head slowly to avoid discomfort or strain.
2. Keep your chin level and shoulders relaxed for proper alignment.

string-array.name: descriptionNeckNeckFlexionStretch
string-array.item: Neck Flexion Stretch
A stretching exercise designed to release tension in the back of the neck and upper shoulders, promoting flexibility and relaxation.
To perform the exercise:
1. Sit or stand upright with your shoulders relaxed.
2. Slowly tilt your head forward, bringing your chin toward your chest.
3. Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds, feeling a gentle pull along the back of your neck.
4. Return to the starting position and repeat as needed.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Avoid forcing your head down to prevent overstretching.
2. Keep your shoulders relaxed and your movements controlled.

string-array.name: descriptionNeckNeckExtensionStretch
string-array.item: Neck Extension Stretch
This stretch targets the front of the neck, promoting better flexibility and releasing tension in the cervical spine.
To perform the exercise:
1. Sit or stand upright with your shoulders relaxed.
2. Slowly tilt your head backward, looking up toward the ceiling.
3. Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds, feeling a gentle stretch along the front of your neck.
4. Return to the starting position and repeat as needed.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Avoid compressing your cervical spine by overextending your neck.
2. Keep the motion slow and controlled to prevent discomfort.

string-array.name: descriptionNeckSideNeckStretch
string-array.item: Side Neck Stretch
A gentle stretch to target the sides of the neck, relieving tension and improving range of motion.
To perform the exercise:
1. Sit or stand upright with your shoulders relaxed.
2. Tilt your head to one side, bringing your ear toward your shoulder.
3. Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds, then switch sides.
4. Repeat as needed on both sides.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Avoid lifting your shoulder to meet your ear; focus on tilting the head only.
2. Perform the stretch slowly to avoid straining the neck muscles.

string-array.name: descriptionNeckSidePushNeckStretch
string-array.item: Side Push Neck Stretch
A stretch that enhances flexibility and releases tension in the sides of the neck by using gentle resistance.
To perform the exercise:
1. Sit or stand upright with your shoulders relaxed.
2. Place one hand on the side of your head and gently push your head toward the opposite shoulder.
3. Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds, then switch sides.
4. Repeat as needed on both sides.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Apply gentle pressure to avoid overstretching or discomfort.
2. Keep your shoulders relaxed throughout the stretch.

string-array.name: descriptionNeckFrontAndBackNeckStretch
string-array.item: Front and Back Neck Stretch
An effective stretch to improve flexibility and relieve stiffness in both the front and back of the neck.
To perform the exercise:
1. Sit or stand upright with your shoulders relaxed.
2. Tilt your head forward, bringing your chin toward your chest, and hold for 15-30 seconds.
3. Tilt your head backward, looking up toward the ceiling, and hold for 15-30 seconds.
4. Repeat as needed to enhance neck mobility.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Move slowly and avoid abrupt motions to prevent strain.
2. Keep your shoulders relaxed and your movements controlled.

string-array.name: descriptionChinTuck
string-array.item: Chin Tuck
The Chin Tuck is a fundamental exercise for improving neck posture and alignment.
This exercise helps counteract forward head posture and strengthens deep neck flexors.
To perform the exercise:
1. Sit or stand with good posture
2. Gently retract chin straight back (not down)
3. Create "double chin" position without tilting head
4. Hold for 5 seconds then release
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep eyes looking forward - don\'t look up or down
2. Use fingers to guide movement initially if needed
3. Perform multiple times throughout day
4. Combine with deep breathing for relaxation

string-array.name: descriptionProneCervicalExtension
string-array.item: Prone Cervical Extension
This exercise strengthens the posterior neck muscles in a controlled manner.
It helps improve neck endurance and postural support.
To perform the exercise:
1. Lie face down on bench with head over edge
2. Start with head in neutral position
3. Slowly lift head to align with torso
4. Lower with control and repeat
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep movement small and controlled
2. Avoid hyperextending or jerking motions
3. Start with bodyweight before adding resistance
4. Combine with chin tucks for balanced training

string-array.name: descriptionKneelingNeckStretch
string-array.item: Kneeling Neck Stretch
This stretch releases tension in the neck and upper trapezius muscles.
It improves mobility and reduces stiffness in the cervical spine.
To perform the exercise:
1. Kneel and place one hand on bench for support
2. Let other arm hang while tilting head opposite side
3. Gently apply overpressure with free hand
4. Hold 20-30 seconds then switch sides
Tips for proper execution:
1. Maintain gentle stretch - no pain
2. Keep shoulders relaxed down
3. Breathe deeply during stretch
4. Combine with shoulder rolls for full release

string-array.name: descriptionWeightedNeckHarnessExtension
string-array.item: Weighted Neck Harness Extension
This exercise builds strength in the posterior neck muscles using specialized equipment.
It\'s commonly used by athletes needing neck stability.
To perform the exercise:
1. Attach appropriate weight to neck harness
2. Lean forward at hips with hands on knees
3. Slowly extend neck against resistance
4. Return to neutral with control
Tips for proper execution:
1. Start with very light weight (2-5 lbs)
2. Maintain smooth, controlled motion
3. Keep movements within comfortable range
4. Balance with flexion exercises

string-array.name: descriptionLyingWeightedNeckFlexion
string-array.item: Lying Weighted Neck Flexion
This exercise strengthens the anterior neck muscles in a supine position.
It helps create balanced neck strength when paired with extension work.
To perform the exercise:
1. Lie on bench with head over edge
2. Place light weight plate on forehead (use towel)
3. Slowly tuck chin to chest against resistance
4. Return to start position with control
Tips for proper execution:
1. Use extremely light weights (1-3 lbs max)
2. Focus on quality of movement over load
3. Keep movements small and precise
4. Combine with isometric holds for variation

string-array.name: descriptionNeckLyingWeightedNeckExtension
string-array.item: Lying Weighted Neck Extension
An exercise to strengthen the posterior neck muscles, improving posture and neck stability.
To perform the exercise:
1. Lie face down on a flat surface with your head extending off the edge and a small weight plate resting on the back of your head.
2. Slowly lift your head upward, extending your neck against the resistance of the weight.
3. Hold for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your head back to the starting position.
4. Repeat for 8-12 repetitions.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Use a light weight initially to avoid overloading the neck muscles.
2. Keep your movements slow and controlled for safety.

string-array.name: descriptionNeckLeverNeckRightSideFlexion
string-array.item: Lever Neck Right Side Flexion (plate loaded)
A targeted exercise to strengthen the lateral neck muscles on the right side, enhancing balance and neck stability.
To perform the exercise:
1. Sit on the lever machine and adjust it to align with the side of your head.
2. Slowly press your head to the side, lifting the weight against resistance.
3. Return to the starting position under control.
4. Repeat for 8-12 repetitions.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Adjust the weight to a manageable level for precise movement.
2. Keep the motion smooth and avoid jerking your head.

string-array.name: descriptionNeckLeverNeckExtension
string-array.item: Lever Neck Extension (plate loaded)
A focused exercise for the posterior neck muscles using a plate-loaded lever machine.
To perform the exercise:
1. Sit on the machine with the pad against the back of your head.
2. Slowly extend your neck backward, lifting the weight against resistance.
3. Pause briefly, then return to the starting position.
4. Repeat for 8-12 repetitions.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Ensure the machine is properly adjusted for your height.
2. Move slowly and steadily to engage the correct muscles.

string-array.name: descriptionNeckCableSeatedNeckFlexion
string-array.item: Cable Seated Neck Flexion with Head Harness
A strengthening exercise for the anterior neck muscles using a cable machine and head harness.
To perform the exercise:
1. Attach the head harness to the cable machine at a low setting and sit facing the machine.
2. Secure the harness around your head and lean slightly forward.
3. Slowly flex your neck, bringing your chin toward your chest against the resistance.
4. Return to the starting position under control.
5. Repeat for 8-12 repetitions.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Keep your back straight and avoid using momentum.
2. Adjust the cable weight to a comfortable level.

string-array.name: descriptionNeckCableSeatedNeckExtension
string-array.item: Cable Seated Neck Extension with Head Harness
An effective exercise to target the posterior neck muscles using a cable machine and head harness.
To perform the exercise:
1. Attach the head harness to the cable machine at a low setting and sit with your back to the machine.
2. Secure the harness around your head and lean slightly forward.
3. Slowly extend your neck backward, lifting the weight against resistance.
4. Return to the starting position under control.
5. Repeat for 8-12 repetitions.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Avoid sudden or jerky movements; keep it slow and controlled.
2. Ensure the harness fits securely for comfort and safety.

string-array.name: descriptionNeckSphinxStretch
string-array.item: Sphinx Stretch
A gentle stretch to target the lower back and improve spinal mobility.
To perform the exercise:
1. Lie face down on the floor with your legs extended and feet hip-width apart.
2. Place your elbows under your shoulders, forearms parallel to each other.
3. Press your forearms into the ground and gently lift your chest, arching your back slightly.
4. Hold the stretch for 20-30 seconds, breathing deeply.
5. Lower back down to the starting position and repeat as needed.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Avoid straining your lower back; keep the lift gentle and controlled.
2. Keep your shoulders relaxed and away from your ears.

string-array.name: descriptionNeckFloorHyperextension
string-array.item: Floor Hyperextension
An exercise to strengthen the lower back, glutes, and hamstrings while improving posture.
To perform the exercise:
1. Lie face down on the floor with your arms extended forward and legs straight.
2. Lift your chest, arms, and legs off the ground simultaneously, squeezing your lower back and glutes.
3. Hold the position briefly, then lower back down to the starting position.
4. Repeat for 10-15 repetitions.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Avoid jerky movements; lift and lower your body smoothly.
2. Keep your neck in a neutral position to prevent strain.

string-array.name: descriptionNeckBhujangasanaCobraAbdominalStretch
string-array.item: Bhujangasana | Cobra Abdominal Stretch
A classic yoga pose to stretch the abdominal muscles and improve spinal flexibility.
To perform the exercise:
1. Lie face down with your hands placed under your shoulders, elbows close to your body.
2. Press your palms into the floor and slowly lift your chest, extending your back.
3. Keep your elbows slightly bent and shoulders relaxed.
4. Hold the position for 20-30 seconds, then return to the starting position.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Avoid overextending your lower back; focus on a comfortable stretch.
2. Engage your glutes and thighs lightly for support.

string-array.name: descriptionNeckFishPose
string-array.item: Fish Pose
A yoga pose that stretches the neck, chest, and shoulders while promoting relaxation.
To perform the exercise:
1. Lie on your back with your legs extended and arms by your sides.
2. Lift your chest upward, arching your back and allowing the top of your head to lightly rest on the ground.
3. Keep your legs and arms relaxed, maintaining the arch for 20-30 seconds.
4. Slowly lower your back and head to return to the starting position.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Avoid putting too much weight on your head; focus on chest elevation.
2. Use a folded blanket under your head for added support if needed.

string-array.name: descriptionNeckSuperman
string-array.item: Superman
An exercise to strengthen the lower back, glutes, and shoulders.
To perform the exercise:
1. Lie face down on the floor with your arms extended forward and legs straight.
2. Simultaneously lift your arms, chest, and legs off the ground, engaging your lower back and glutes.
3. Hold the position for 2-3 seconds, then slowly lower back down.
4. Repeat for 10-15 repetitions.
Tips for proper execution:
1. Avoid jerking movements; keep the lift and lower controlled.
2. Focus on squeezing your glutes and keeping your neck neutral.
